summary: PEAD does not pass: 0 of 8 registered cells. Events = 32,452 eligible earnings reactions from 186,543 SEC 8-K Item 2.02 filings mapped to 4,232 bar tickers (TEST 2015-01..2026-08: 24,784 events; timing 52% post-close, 46% pre-open, 3% intraday), universe prev close >= $5 and ADV20 >= $50M, entry Open_{R+1}, tier costs, net of SPY, wider-of-day/quarter cluster CI. Top-quintile earnings reactions (C1) earn -0.17% over 5 sessions and +0.10% over 20 (CIs straddle zero, Holm p 1.0). The big-beat proxy C2 (reaction >= +8%, volume >= 3x) is +0.75%/20d with lower CI -0.44% and Holm p 0.52; the most-liquid tercile C5 is +0.76%/20d, lower CI -0.23%, Holm 0.40; the small/mid cell C4 is +0.00%. The strongest family member is the SHORT side of bottom-quintile reactions (C3: +0.40%/5d, +0.66%/20d short-side, unadjusted p 0.03, Holm 0.21-0.22, lower CI -0.02/-0.01, 67-83% of years positive) but matched non-event names with the same day-0 drop drift down just as much (control excess +0.11%/-0.45% registered match; -0.30%/+0.40% any-decile match, all CIs through zero), so it is the move, not the news. News-or-move for C1: on the 62% of events with any-decile controls, earnings-tagged names beat matched movers by +0.26% (5d, [-0.27,+0.88]) and +0.38% (20d, [-1.34,+2.37]); the C1 events themselves are negative on that subset. Post-close announcers drift more than pre-open ones (C1 h20 post +0.39% vs pre -0.31%) but no timing slice clears zero. K=10 per-capital series underperform SPY buy-and-hold (C1 h20: CAGR +9.2%, max DD -52% vs SPY +12.0%/-34%; C2: +10.0%, -33%). 2025-2026 are negative for every long cell. Unregistered post-hoc observation for a future registration: the session after the reaction day continues the move for extremes (C3 short-side +0.27% [+0.14,+0.40], C2 +0.28% [+0.04,+0.53], one session), again mostly matched by non-event movers. Conclusion: knowing an earnings release happened, its timing and its price reaction does not create a tradeable drift after 10-20 bp costs on this universe; the remaining untested lever is the content of the release (beat size, guidance), not the fact of it.

Post-close announcers drift up more than pre-open ones on the long side (consistent with the overnight-accrual finding: the pre-open reporter has already had its overnight leg before R's close), but no long slice clears zero after Holm-free CIs.
caveats: Survivorship: symbol list as of 2026-09, delisted names absent; flatters long cells and understates the C3 short side (the failed shorts that went to zero are missing).

Registered matched-control rule (same date, same ADV decile, |day-0 excess| <= 1 pp, no 8-K +-5 sessions) covers only 23% of C1, 22% of C3 and 6% of C2 events; the control statistic is therefore weak and its covered subset is skewed to smaller reactions. The any-decile sensitivity (84% overall, 62% of C1, 30% of C2) is reported separately and is not part of the pass test.
Month-quintile threshold uses events later in the same calendar month (mild look-ahead); the trailing-250-event threshold variant gives the same answer (C1_trail h5 -0.13, h20 +0.07).

Panel composition shifts: ~1,000 tickers exist only in bars1d_all (2024-09 onward), so eligible events per year jump from 2,449 (2024) to 4,245 (2025); the 7-session hole 2024-09-03..11 drops trades needing those bars; 2004-2013 panel has 1,225 names and 8-K 2.02 coverage before ~2008 is incomplete.
C3 is evaluated as a short with the same tier costs and no borrow fee or hard-to-borrow constraint.

CIK->ticker mapping takes the first SEC-listed ticker with a bar file (dual-class names counted once); 8-K/A excluded (1,619); 3,900 filings dropped as duplicates within 5 sessions; 2.7% of events are intraday filings (flagged 'intra', signal still taken at R's close).
Horizon-20/60 windows overlap heavily; the quarter-cluster CI (always the wider one) is the relevant interval and it never clears zero for a long cell.
The h=1 continuation observations (C3 short +0.27%, C2 +0.28%) are post-hoc and unregistered; matched controls explain most of them; they must not be read as a pass.
Per-capital K=10 is capacity-bound in earnings season (77% of C1 events skipped), so the equity curve measures capacity as much as signal; it uses fixed 1/K weights and no SPY hedge.
Costs are 10/20 bp round trip by ADV tier only; no slippage beyond that, no borrow, no financing.
